The Transformation Fund is an active bursary program by Daughters of Tomorrow that provides working women with up to $10,000 to support further study or training. It aims to help women take the next step in their careers without financial burden. Eligibility includes being employed in the current role for at least 6 months, having a clear plan to stay employed while studying, being a first-time applicant to the fund, and not currently receiving another DOT bursary. Preference is given to applicants whose course relates to their current industry and those with a gross income of $2,900 or below. The program involves commitment to completing the course, pursuing a sustainable career, participating in check-ins, and sharing experiences with DOT.

The Kampong Kapor Family Service Centre (KKFSC) is active and provides support services including information and referrals, casework and counselling, group work, and community work. It serves as a welcoming first touchpoint for those seeking guidance and offers longer-term support to strengthen family relationships and build resilience. The centre is located at Blk 2 Kitchener Road #03-89, Lift Lobby B, Singapore 200002, with operating hours Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from 9:00am to 6:00pm, and Tuesday and Thursday from 9:00am to 9:00pm. Contact details include telephone 6485 4720 and email kkfsc@kkcs.org.sg.

The DOT Confidence Curriculum is an active flagship program by Daughters of Tomorrow designed to help women rebuild confidence and practical workplace skills as they prepare to return to work. The program offers a supportive environment where clients rediscover their strengths, build communication and workplace skills, and connect with other women on similar journeys. Sessions are conducted in English with onsite childminding provided. Interested individuals are encouraged to speak with their social worker or get in touch with the organization for more information.

The Return-to-Work (RTW) programme by ABLE supports clients who want to return to work by providing career coaching, job placement, transferable skills development, and on-the-job training. It helps individuals find new, suitable, and sustainable employment or return to existing jobs with a seamless transition. The program is individualized and includes therapeutic, psychosocial, and employability support to enable clients to be independent and reintegrate into the community successfully. This program appears to be the current active employment-related scheme, likely replacing the previous EmploymentABLE scheme.

The 'Access Services' program provides a safe, supervised environment where parents and caregivers can rebuild connections with their children placed in alternative care. It offers supervised access to facilitate reunification, parenting coaching, counseling, and social work support. The program operates under the Ministry of Social & Family Development’s authorization and aims to heal and strengthen family bonds in a safe environment. This program appears to be the current active equivalent or replacement of the previously named 'Trauma Access' program.
